result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.bipartite_sets()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page doc-py-api-page shift-heading-level-by: 0 toc-depth: 3 page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Return the two node partitions of a bipartite graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L5671-L5708){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.bipartite_sets() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Uses BFS 2-coloring to partition nodes into two independent sets such that every edge connects nodes from different sets. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [tuple[list[int], list[int]]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A pair of lists containing the node IDs of each partition. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If the graph is not bipartite. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#50b963ce .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph() .add_node(label="Gene1") .add_node(label="Gene2") .add_node(label="Disease1") .add_node(label="Disease2") .add_edge("Gene1", "Disease1") .add_edge("Gene1", "Disease2") .add_edge("Gene2", "Disease1") ) set_a, set_b = graph.bipartite_sets() len(set_a), len(set_b) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` (2, 2) ``` ::: :::
